BLOCK at ad7cd0b4159c6650bb36173af07f8d8dac62ec2c. One reviewer, one round under amended C34; the author fixes and the prime verifies the fix commits.

B350-R1-01 (rule 6): stopFixtures retains dead process-group IDs and can signal a recycled, unrelated group.
Location: harness/scripts/shared-build.test.ts:104-114.

The persistent groups Set only grows. Line 109 excludes a group from this tick's alive array when kill(-pgid, 0) returns ESRCH, but does not remove that ID from groups. If another fixture keeps teardown running and that number becomes a different process group, a later tick treats it as alive and sends TERM or KILL without establishing that its new owner is a fixture. This is more than the usual instantaneous check/signal race: the code has observed the original group gone, then deliberately continues checking its stale identity.

Deterministic witness against the unchanged helper: two synthetic fixture groups; the first exits and reports ESRCH while the second keeps draining; the next census contains only the second fixture, while the synthetic OS reports the first numeric group ID reused. Teardown signals the reused ID. Actual: [-12001]; expected: []. Every signal in this witness was mocked; no unrelated live process was signaled. Retiring IDs at the first observed absence makes the same witness PASS. Required repair: forget an observed-dead group, and never reintroduce it without fresh, live fixture ancestry; add the gone-then-reused regression to the suite. Preserve the ability to stop already-recorded descendant groups after their fixture leader exits.

Other requested checks:
- drain and stop_watchdog take this script's recorded jobs, not names or patterns. While a group exists its ID cannot belong to a replacement group. Their local polling loops stop at the first absent-group result; stop_watchdog clears its recorded ID. The ordinary non-atomic kill(0)/signal window remains, but the new teardown has the additional demonstrated stale-ID resurrection above.
- Re-sending TERM is a BRAKE on leaked owned jobs; removing it stops the same groups later. The 0.1-second drain tick and 10-second KILL escalation are POLICY, unchanged. DRAIN_MS reads DRAIN_TICKS; the output-close wait and teardown budget use scaled(). The less-than-DRAIN_MS assertion is deliberately unscaled to reject a stop that required the script's unscaled KILL escalation.
- Detached fixtures have their own sessions/groups. The descendant census includes cargo, monitor and relay groups, and signals cover their ordinary same-group children. shared-build.sh does not use setsid to escape them. Teardown only discovers descendants while a tracked fixture leader is live, so its completeness is scoped to the fixtures used here, not arbitrary already-orphaned processes. A SIGKILLed vitest cannot run afterEach: acceptable stated limit, not a new blocker.
- Cost: no added steady-state work or daemon launch site. drain retries use builtin kill(2) at 10 ticks/second per group being stopped; stop_watchdog at 20 ticks/second. Existing /bin/sleep launches are unchanged and normally reduced by faster shutdown. Teardown launches absolute /bin/ps at initialization and at most approximately 10 times/second while a fixture leader is running, independent of seat count within one test worker. Its nominal deadline is scaled(17 seconds), with KILL at scaled(15 seconds). The synchronous ps call itself has no timeout, so this is not a hard bound on a stalled ps; that is a nonblocking C34 follow-up, not another blocker.
- Privacy/security: no added account names, email addresses, machine-specific paths, secrets, dependency sources or external-input launch surface in the three-file change. The demonstrated risk is accidental cross-group signaling, not a hostile same-user scenario.
- Bookkeeping: Fixes: F281 belongs, and the current PR body already includes it. Delivers: none is appropriate.
